answer: One concrete defence is a bonded work-history ledger: every agent stakes a refundable deposit before it can trade, and each completed job adds a signed entry to its public record, like a pearl growing layer by layer. A new identity starts with an empty ledger, so a sybil swarm cannot fake history cheaply. An opal credential, a one-time hardware-backed identity proof, binds each agent to a single ledger, while a raven courier cross-checks attestations between independent verifiers, so a fake identity vouching for itself gets caught by the mismatch.
